doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Praise of Mary, Cannery Row and the Clint Eastwood documentary
summary: Major unrecorded works and plans to include Cannery Row as a bonus in the Eastwood film.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: These are the kind of things that aren’t recorded. The Praise of Mary Canticles haven’t been recorded. These are 35-, 40 minute . . .
These are major compositions of yours that most people haven’t had a chance to hear.
Then this bunch of new things will be recorded.
The Cannery Row work that you performed at Monterey – has that been recorded?
No.
That’s another one that I’ve read reviews of, but haven’t had a chance to hear the music. A lot of people would like to hear this.
It could be . . .
The live performance was recorded, and actually, it’s well enough recorded . . .
It could be commercially released.
I’d love to see that. Clint Eastwood had cameras there. He’s doing a documentary on me.
My next question was going to be to ask you about that.
I keep saying, “Are you going to use Cannery Row?” – through the people in his staff – “Are you going to use Cannery Row in the documentary?” They said, “We’ll use it
as bookends.” I said, “It’s such a good first and only performance, that I would very much like you to do the whole thing.”
That could be an extra feature on the DVD. Now that they have DVDs, they have an extra feature. They could just have the whole performance there.
You just said the answer.
Oh, Is that so? Great minds think alike.
That’s how they answered me. What’d they call it? A bonus.
A bonus feature. That would be great.

“We’ll put it on the end.” They said, “If it’s so important to you, we’d like you to know that we’ve thought of a way. We’ll put it as a complete piece as a bonus.” I don’t know how that works. Maybe you do.
That’ll be great. That will get great visibility. A lot of people will see it.
It will? I’m so anxious to see that.
